<USER_SCRIPT>
CORAL — A CITY LAUNCH

INT. DOWNTOWN APARTMENT BATHROOM - MORNING

Hard light off white tile. SCARLETT,
a city influencer in a black turtleneck,
unboxes a coral lipstick and turns it slowly to camera.

SCARLETT (V.O.)
One shade. One city.

CLOSE ON THE TUBE — the coral bullet twists up and catches the
light. Scarlett smiles at her reflection, the colour already hers.

EXT. DOWNTOWN SIDEWALK - CONTINUOUS

Scarlett walks a crowded crosswalk, taxis stacked at the light,
office glass behind her. She glances back at camera.

SCARLETT (V.O.)
Made for the street. Wear it everywhere.

EXT. ROOFTOP LEDGE - CONTINUOUS

She laughs as a train rattles past below. The lipstick lands
beside the brand mark on the concrete ledge.

SUPER:  CORAL.  OUT NOW.
</USER_SCRIPT>

Target video duration: 1 minute (about 8-12 clips). Group clips that share a location and beat into one scene — a scene may hold several shots. Each SHOT is one video clip. Clip durations MUST be 5–15 seconds — those are the only lengths the selected video model can render. Label every scene (e.g. a "Scene 3 — 5s" heading). When a scene has more than one shot, also label each shot (e.g. "Shot 1 — 5s"); shot labels in a scene MUST add up to the scene label. A one-shot scene needs only the scene label — that label IS the clip duration. The clip labels (shot labels when present, otherwise scene labels) MUST add up to 60 seconds (±2 seconds). Count the clips, add the labels, and do not return until they sum to the target. Reach the target through the number of shots, not by stretching illegal clip lengths. If the brief asks for a title card, logo, SUPER, or on-screen text, do not write that card — the image model cannot render text. Substitute a final living beat with a real subject. End with a single line: TOTAL: <sum>s

Style & genre (let this drive WHAT HAPPENS, not just the look):
- Style: Product Ad / ecommerce
- About: Fresh, tactile product content with lifestyle context and sensory detail. Designed for Instagram, DTC brands, e-commerce, and social-first campaigns.
- Genre cues: ecommerce, product, instagram, dtc, lifestyle, social

Style context (apply these aesthetics throughout):
- Mood: Fresh, sensory, and effortlessly cool
- Art style: Modern social-first product photography with tactile, editorial energy. Products shown in real-life context -- hands opening packaging, fingers pressing textures, products on bathroom shelves, kitchen counters, rumpled linen. Close-up detail shots emphasize material and finish. Flat-lays with curated minimal arrangements. Color-matched backgrounds that complement the product. Every frame feels like something you would screenshot and save
- Lighting: Bright natural window light with clean directional shadows. Direct on-camera flash for punchy editorial energy on select shots. No heavy diffusion -- let light feel real and immediate. Warm late-afternoon glow for lifestyle moments. High-key and airy overall with pops of contrast
- Color palette: #FFFFFF, #F0E6D3, #D4536D, #1A1A1A, #E8F4E8
- Color grading: Clean and bright with true-to-life color. Whites are crisp, skin tones warm and natural. Minimal processing -- the product looks like it does in your hand. Slight warmth in highlights, lifted shadows keeping everything airy. One accent color pops against neutral base
- Camera work: Dynamic mix of handheld and locked shots with consistent energy. Handheld with natural micro-movement for lifestyle moments -- hands interacting, daily rituals, real context. Quick-cut to locked beauty frames for hero product shots. Macro details on textures and surfaces. Overhead flat-lays directly above. Eye-level and slightly above angles. Shallow depth of field on tactile details. Energetic pacing -- no lingering, every frame earns its time
- Reference works: modern social-first skincare-brand content, dewy minimalist beauty-brand visual identity, sun-soaked lifestyle beauty campaigns, playful color-blocked skincare content

Aspect ratio: 16:9 landscape — favor wide, cinematic compositions

response.content:
Scene 1 — 18s — Downtown Apartment Bathroom, Morning

Shot 1 — 6s

Hard morning light cuts across white tile and a black stone sink. Scarlett, a sharp-eyed city influencer in a black turtleneck, tears open a coral-colored lipstick carton with one hand while her phone vibrates beside the faucet. She ignores the phone, focused on the small ritual; handheld camera drifts closer over her shoulder.

Shot 2 — 6s

Her fingers twist the lipstick upward. The coral bullet catches a clean stripe of sunlight as she turns it between thumb and forefinger, the matte surface contrasting with glossy white tile. The camera makes a quick, precise macro push-in while her other hand steadies the tube.

Shot 3 — 6s

Scarlett applies the color in the bathroom mirror, then hears a distant subway rumble and pauses mid-smile. She checks the time on her phone, grabs her black sunglasses, and says softly to her reflection, “Okay. City’s waiting.” She sweeps out of frame as the camera holds on the vivid coral against the neutral room.

Scene 2 — 12s — Apartment Hallway and Stairwell

Shot 1 — 6s

Scarlett strides through a narrow downtown hallway, lipstick in one hand and a canvas tote in the other. She snaps the tube shut while moving, slips it into the tote, then doubles back to retrieve her phone from a radiator shelf. The handheld camera tracks backward in front of her, keeping her face and coral lips crisp against cream walls.

Shot 2 — 6s

In a sunlit concrete stairwell, Scarlett descends two flights at a brisk pace, one hand sliding along the black rail. A shaft of light flashes across her face with each landing; she catches her reflection in a small wired-glass window and turns her chin toward it, amused, before continuing down. The camera pans with her energetic movement.

Scene 3 — 18s — Downtown Crosswalk, Late Morning

Shot 1 — 6s

A wide 16:9 street composition: Scarlett steps into a crowded crosswalk among commuters, yellow taxis, delivery bikes, and mirrored office towers. She walks against the flow with relaxed purpose, coral lips the only bright color in her black-and-neutral outfit. The camera tracks sideways at pedestrian pace as traffic begins rolling behind her.

Shot 2 — 6s

At the curb, a gust catches the loose strap of Scarlett’s tote. She hooks it with her elbow without breaking stride, then pulls the coral lipstick from the bag and checks the bullet in the reflection of a parked car window. The camera swings from her moving hand to her face as the city streaks softly behind her.

Shot 3 — 6s

Scarlett reaches the far side just as the walk signal changes. She turns back toward camera while still moving, raises the lipstick like a tiny baton, and grins. A taxi glides through the background, sunlight flashing across its windows. She says, “Same city. Better color,” then disappears into a stream of office workers.

Scene 4 — 12s — Rooftop Above Downtown, Late Afternoon

Shot 1 — 6s

On a rooftop beside low concrete walls and potted grasses, Scarlett opens the lipstick again while wind lifts a few strands of her hair. She presses the tube into her palm, applies one quick touch-up using the dark reflection of her phone, and laughs as an elevated train rattles across the distant skyline. The camera arcs around her, keeping the coral shade vivid against pale sky and glass towers.

Shot 2 — 6s

Scarlett places the closed lipstick on the rooftop ledge, then immediately reaches back for it as the wind nudges it toward the edge. She catches it, looks at the camera with a knowing smile, and tucks it safely into her pocket before walking toward the glowing skyline. The camera holds low and tracks beside her moving silhouette, ending on her coral lips as she turns into the warm late-afternoon light.

TOTAL: 60s
